speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: When I compare this with the corresponding figures for previous years, I note that there were 12,000-over in 2015, and about 11,900 in 2014.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Percentage wise, the Parliamentary Secretary mentioned that it was 16% for 2016.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: This is a big drop from the earlier percentages of 25% in 2015 and 35% in 2014.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: To me, these figures do not look very encouraging.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Or are employers not approving or not encouraging fathers to apply?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What is the Civil Service going to do about it?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If members look at the actual take-up rate, in fact, it has gone up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But like I said earlier, fathers have up to 12 months to take the paternity leave from the date of the birth of their child.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: On the other hand, the employer has three months more to submit the claims.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The figures for 2015 and 2016 have not been finalised and we expect the figures to be higher.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: If you look back, the trend has been going up, and it is encouraging.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As for the Civil Service, the 16% is with regard to the total applications.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But if you look at the numbers and figures for the Civil Service, in fact, they have also been creeping up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Again, similar to what I said earlier, we have not reached the cut-off dates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We expect the percentage to go up further, which is very encouraging.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We are very committed to encouraging fathers to be part of the family development and child-raising process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: At the same time, there are all the different platforms and initiatives undertaken to provide opportunities for fathers to play a role, not only from Government, but also from community organisations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I am very heartened that Members like Mr Seah and Mr Louis Ng, and my own Minister Tan Chuan-Jin, are trying to promote active fathering.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I think this is something that we should develop further.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We should harness this within our society so that the whole spectrum of fathering becomes part and parcel of the process of family development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I believe this will help to strengthen our families and will somehow enhance the development of our society.
